newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister suspends Istanbul police chief.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister suspends Istanbul police chief.

text.p: Turkey's Interior Minister Meral Aksener said on Thursday she had suspended Istanbul police chief Kemal Yazicioglu and five other security force members to help investigations into the murder of a casino boss.
Aksener told a news conference that the measure was taken after opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz said casino owner Omer Lutfu Topal was killed by three Istanbul police officers.

"There are contradictions between their statements and information given by the Istanbul police chief. I am suspending them from their duties as of today for the benefit of the investigation," she said.

Aksener said the government must take seriously assertions by Yilmaz, a former prime minister, that the three police officers confessed on video that they murdered Topal, Turkey's "casino king", in July.
"Claims made in connection with the murder of Topal have reached the point where they have seriously unsettled both the state and public opinion," Aksener told reporters.
The deputy Istanbul police chief, the head of a special security force and three police officers were suspended alongside Yazicioglu.

State-run Anatolian news agency said the three policemen were bodyguards of Sedat Bucak, a Kurdish tribal chief and MP who was injured last month in a car crash in which a senior police officer and a wanted gangster both died in the same car.
Bucak gave information to a Turkish prosecutor this week about the incident which has erupted into a full-blown scandal in Turkey linking the state with organised crime.
Former interior minister Mehmet Agar resigned after news of the scandal emerged and Aksener succeeded him in the post.
Turkish newspapers said Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan met Yazicioglu and Aksener on Wednesday to discuss the speculation about Topal's death.
